topic: isolation boundaries by execution mode: how container, nspawn, VM, and unit modes differ in what they isolate and which threats each boundary answers

subtopics.scope: What a rootless podman container isolates: user/mount/PID/network namespaces, cgroups, the default seccomp profile, and which threats the container wall answers (escape, escalation, image tampering).
seed_queries: podman rootless containers isolation namespaces seccomp
container security threat model namespaces cgroups seccomp

subtopics.scope: systemd-nspawn as a boundary: user namespace mapping with --private-users, ephemeral overlay mode (--ephemeral), boot-in-container, and discard-at-exit semantics.
The VM boundary (QEMU/KVM, bcvk): hardware virtualization isolation vs containers, libvirt default NAT network virbr0, ephemeral disk images, and why a VM answers threats containers cannot.
seed_queries: QEMU KVM virtual machine isolation vs containers threat model
libvirt default network virbr0 NAT isolation

subtopics.scope: The systemd unit sandbox as a persistent-daemon boundary: SystemCallFilter, PrivateTmp, RuntimeDirectory, ProtectSystem/ProtectHome, NoNewPrivileges, and what each directive answers.
seed_queries: systemd service sandboxing SystemCallFilter PrivateTmp ProtectSystem
systemd unit hardening directives RuntimeDirectory NoNewPrivileges

subtopics.scope: Execution mode semantics: one-shot (--rm), ephemeral (--ephemeral), persistent (systemd unit), destructive one-shot (disk flash); lifetime, cleanup contract, and exit-rc propagation per mode.
seed_queries: docker run --rm cleanup semantics exit code
systemd-nspawn ephemeral overlay discarded on exit

subtopics.scope: Mode-specific hazards: state leaks after interrupted cleanup (orphaned network namespaces, virbr0 left UP), restart-expectation bugs under PrivateTmp/RuntimeDirectory, and confirmation gates for destructive one-shot modes (bootc install to-disk vs to-filesystem).
seed_queries: bootc install to-disk destructive wipe confirmation
systemd RuntimeDirectory removed on stop state loss

subtopics.scope: Privilege model across modes: rootless user namespaces as the container/nspawn constant, sudo/KVM escalation for VM rows, and per-mode seccomp application (podman default profile, nspawn --system-call-filter, unit SystemCallFilter=@system-service).

Where observers and secrets sit relative to boundaries: eBPF measurement daemons (Falco, Tetragon) running in persistent mode to observe containers and VMs, eBPF visibility limits inside VMs, and keeping hardware secrets (YubiKey) outside every boundary.
seed_queries: Tetragon Falco eBPF security monitoring containers visibility
eBPF runtime security monitoring host vs VM boundary
